findings.claim: The data-type check rejects any T where `type.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`. A type that comes from a referenced assembly through a metadata (DLL) reference has no declaring syntax references. So the case the requirement exists for (ProjectA.MyType compiled into a referenced DLL, formatter declared in Project B) gets MsgPack021 and no generated formatter. The annotated class keeps no implementation, and the build fails with CS0535. Only same-compilation types, or types reached through CompilationReference, ever pass this check.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.FormatterForTypeInReferencedAssemblyWithoutMessagePack_IsGenerated. It compiles ProjectA without MessagePack, emits it to an image and references it via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. Expect it to fail on head with an MsgPack021 generator diagnostic and no 'partial class MyObjectFormatter' in the generated sources.

findings.claim: The acceptance criteria say that if T carries MessagePack attributes ([MessagePackObject]/[Key], or [DataContract]/[DataMember]) they are honoured, and that contractless mode applies only when those attributes are absent. With no surrogate, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers. That path never inspects T's attributes, so any T is serialized as public read-write members keyed by name. Keys, Order/Name, IgnoreMember and DataContract opt-in membership are all ignored, and members that T excludes are still serialized.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementTests.FormatterHonoursDataContractOnFormattedType. T is a [DataContract] type with one [DataMember(Order = 0)] property and one unannotated 'Secret' property. Expect head to fail because the generated formatter references 'Secret'.
